answer: One deed, one agent. The land registry ties each property to a named owner, so use it as the bridge between a wallet and a real person. First, the agent presents its deed number and name. Second, the network checks the public registry: deed active, name matches. Third, that deed locks to one identity and cannot back a second. A farm wanting a thousand fakes needs a thousand properties at $2,500 in fees and six weeks per deed, so $2.5 million vanishes before any reward. A fake is cheap to type and ruinous to deed, like a falcon circling a marble courtyard forever without owning a stone.
